answer: A farm that floods the queue early thus gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the sparrow ordering is published with the pigment batch, the horizon audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 57% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 126 account operation therefore ties up 40 million dollars of idle capital. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
